title: AI-Based Wealth Advisory System using Machine Learning and Predictive Analytics for Personalized Budget Planning
authors: Bhavana B R; D Pavan; Guru Darshan T H
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Computer Science & Technology
tldr: AI Wealth Advisor integrates classification, forecasting, anomaly detection, and explainable AI to deliver personalized budget planning with 95% anomaly detection accuracy and 22% savings improvement.
problem_and_motivation: Most personal finance applications remain reactive, focusing on expense tracking rather than proactive wealth management. Over 60% of adults worldwide lack understanding of fundamental financial concepts. AI-driven financial tools remain enterprise-focused, creating a gap in personalized consumer-centric advisory solutions.
approach: Proposed AI Wealth Advisor, a multi-model architecture integrating classification, forecasting, anomaly detection, and explainable AI for personalized financial guidance.
Used XGBoost and Random Forests for expense classification on structured transaction data, with BERT-based NLP models for unstructured descriptions.
Employed ARIMA, Prophet, LSTM, and Transformers in an ensemble forecasting framework to predict future expenditure.
Applied Isolation Forests, Autoencoders, and GAN-based detectors for fraud and anomaly detection in spending behavior.
Integrated Contextual Bandits and Reinforcement Learning to dynamically adjust personalized budget recommendations.
Leveraged SHAP and LIME for model interpretability, translating complex analytics into natural language explanations.
Addressed the cold-start problem using household expenditure surveys as generalized benchmarks for new users.
Conducted a pilot study with 100 users to validate expense classification, forecasting accuracy, anomaly detection, and recommendation adoption.
findings: num: 91% F1-score for expense classification accuracy.
num: 22% improvement in savings among pilot study participants.
num: 78% of participants reported enhanced financial literacy.
num: Forecasting error of $43/month per user (MAE).
num: Hybrid ARIMA-GBDT models reduced mean absolute error by 18% in household expenditure predictions.
num: Autoencoders with Isolation Forest achieved 96% fraud detection accuracy in prior work.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Literature review summary of 15 AI/ML methods in finance -> surveys, autoencoders, and deep learning dominate prior work.

definitions.definition: Explainable AI, providing transparency in black-box model predictions.
Natural Language Generation, translating analytics into user-friendly text.
Long Short-Term Memory network for non-linear time-series forecasting.
Mean Absolute Error, measuring average forecasting deviation.
SHapley Additive exPlanations, providing consistent feature attributions.
Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations for model transparency.
General Data Protection Regulation, EU data privacy framework.
Advanced Encryption Standard with 256-bit key for data-at-rest encryption.
Gradient Boosted Decision Trees, an ensemble learning method.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper presents AI Wealth Advisor, a multi-component architecture that unifies expense classification, time-series forecasting, anomaly detection, and explainable AI within a single personal finance advisory system.
directly_justifies: AI Wealth Advisor integrates classification, forecasting, anomaly detection, and explainable AI for personalized budget planning.
num: Pilot study demonstrated 95% anomaly detection accuracy and 91% expense classification F1-score.
num: Users showed 22% improvement in savings and 78% reported enhanced financial literacy.
Cold-start problem addressed through generalized expenditure survey benchmarks for new users.
XAI integration via SHAP and LIME translates complex analytics into natural language explanations.
limits: The paper presents a proposed system architecture rather than a deployed, peer-reviewed implementation with reproducible code.
Pilot study involves only 100 users without specifying demographic diversity or duration of the study.
The paper conflates literature review findings with the proposed system's own results, making it unclear which outcomes are directly measured.
No comparative evaluation against existing commercial personal finance tools is provided.
Generalizability across different financial ecosystems and currencies is not empirically validated.
